newsitem.title: UK: UK petrol margins continue strangulation - analyst.
newsitem.headline: UK petrol margins continue strangulation - analyst.

text.p: U.K. retail petrol margins continued to narrow in the last few weeks and remained in the basement of European rankings as the summer driving season approached, according to independent analysts Oil Price Assessments Ltd (OPAL).
Gross retail margins for unleaded petrol narrowed to 3.9 pence per litre as of April 25 from March's average of 4.1 pence and 4.7 pence in mid-February, said Peter Regnier, director of OPAL.
Current margins are still healthier than year-ago levels of 1.6 pence right after Esso Petroleum, a unit of U.S. oil giant Exxon Corp, launched its Pricewatch campaign.
Esso promised to match its lowest-priced competitors in a downstream sector in Great Britain already plagued by overcapacity and a growing presence of the low-cost hypermarkets.
"It's still very, very competitive and margins on average are lower here than any other European country," Regnier said. "The price war is less intense than a year ago but it is still very tough."
He said a realignment can occur on the street within 30 minutes, so it is virtually impossible to determine who is driving prices lower.
